sector: Materials - Diversified Metals & Mining / Mining Services
overview: Mineral Resources Limited (MinRes) is a Western Australia-based diversified mining and mining-services company, founded and led by Chris Ellison since it listed on the ASX in 2006. It operates an integrated 'build-own-operate' model spanning a large third-party and internal Mining Services business (crushing, haulage, port and infrastructure), iron ore production (the flagship Onslow Iron project plus the legacy Pilbara Hub), hard-rock lithium (Wodgina, Mt Marion, and the restarted Bald Hill), and an emerging Energy (gas exploration) business in the Perth and Carnarvon basins. FY26 (year ended 30 June 2026) was a record year, with revenue of $6,461M (+44%) and statutory NPAT of $1,061M (+217%), driven by Onslow Iron reaching 35Mtpa nameplate capacity, record Mining Services earnings, and a lithium price recovery.

business_model.summary: MinRes' distinguishing 'razor and razor blades' model is Mining Services: it designs, builds, owns and operates crushing, haulage and infrastructure assets under long-life contracts (>85% life-of-mine, many 15+ years with CPI indexation) for third-party miners, its own joint ventures, and its own wholly-owned mines. This non-cyclical, high-retention services base underpins earnings through commodity cycles, while the company also takes direct commodity price exposure through its own iron ore and lithium production, which drives the bulk of earnings volatility. Growth capital has historically been recycled via partial asset sales (e.g., the Onslow Iron haul road sale to Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners, and the pending POSCO lithium JV) rather than solely equity raises.

revenue_streams.name: Mining Services
revenue_streams.note: Record FY26 Underlying EBITDA of $976M; ~305-325Mt FY26 production guidance; considered the 'non-cyclical' earnings anchor

revenue_streams.name: Iron Ore (Onslow Iron + Pilbara Hub)
revenue_streams.note: Onslow Iron reached 35Mtpa nameplate in August 2025, targeting ~40Mtpa in FY27; Iron Ore Underlying EBITDA $573M in 1H26 alone

revenue_streams.name: Lithium (Wodgina, Mt Marion, Bald Hill)
revenue_streams.note: Lithium Underlying EBITDA swung from near-breakeven/negative in FY24-25 to $167M in 1H26 on higher spodumene prices; Bald Hill restarted in FY26

revenue_streams.name: Energy (Perth/Carnarvon Basin gas)
revenue_streams.note: Perth Basin exploration success; $780M upfront payment received from Hancock Prospecting for permit sale/JV formation in FY25, plus contingent payments in FY26

business_model.customer_type: B2B — mining services contracts with Tier 1 miners and joint-venture partners; commodity sales (iron ore, spodumene concentrate) to global steel and battery supply chains, predominantly China
business_model.geographic_mix: Operations concentrated in Western Australia (Pilbara and Yilgarn regions); revenue/product sales largely into Asian (principally Chinese) steel and battery-materials markets

competitive_position.market_position: A mid-tier but fast-growing diversified miner; not a scale peer of BHP/Rio Tinto/Fortescue in iron ore, but differentiated by its vertically integrated Mining Services capability. In lithium hard-rock concentrate, MinRes is one of the largest global producers (with Pilbara Minerals and Greenbushes/IGO-Tianqi) and, following the Bald Hill restart, the world's only operator of three hard-rock lithium mines with their own spodumene concentrate facilities.

moat_factors.description: In-house engineering/construction and mining services capability lets MinRes unlock stranded, remote deposits (e.g., Onslow Iron's private 150km haul road, purpose-built port and transhipper fleet) faster and cheaper than peers who must contract out
>85% of Mining Services contracts are life-of-mine, many 15+ years with CPI indexation; only two contracts lost in 10 years (both won back), giving recurring, non-cyclical earnings
Onslow Iron FOB costs of ~$52/wmt (1H26) position it as a low-cost, long-life iron ore operation; Wodgina/Mt Marion are considered world-class lithium ore bodies
History of selling down stakes (haul road to MSIP, Perth Basin gas permits to Hancock, pending 30% lithium stake to POSCO) to fund growth and delever without pure equity dilution

Chris Ellison's hands-on, fast-moving culture has driven project delivery (Onslow Iron built in under two years) but is also the source of the governance/related-party controversies that damaged trust

weaknesses: High historical net debt and reliance on commodity price cycles for two of three core segments (iron ore, lithium)
Governance overhang: founder/MD Chris Ellison's related-party dealings and prior tax non-disclosure issues damaged reputation and led to board/leadership churn
Concentration in Western Australia single-jurisdiction operations and predominantly Chinese offtake markets
Execution risk on major growth capital projects (Onslow Iron haul road damage during commissioning was a recent example)
Historically inconsistent/absent dividend (no dividends FY23-FY25) reflecting balance sheet strain

growth_drivers: Onslow Iron ramp beyond 35Mtpa nameplate towards ~40Mtpa in FY27 as additional transhippers (6th and 7th) arrive, with FOB costs trending to the low end of guidance
Mining Services volume growth (FY26 record; FY26 guidance of 305-325Mt, ~12.5% growth) as Onslow Iron and new third-party/JV contracts scale, approaching ~$1bn annualised EBITDA
Lithium price recovery (SC6 spodumene up sharply through 2026) directly re-rating Wodgina, Mt Marion and the restarted Bald Hill operations

POSCO Holdings lithium JV: US$765M upfront cash for a 30% interest in the Wodgina/Mt Marion lithium business (agreement executed May 2026, expected to complete in H1 FY27), funding further deleveraging and validating asset value (~$3.9bn implied value for MinRes' existing 50% interests)
Pilbara Hub transition from higher-cost Wonmunna to the lower-cost, longer-life Lamb Creek deposit (first ore expected 2H26/FY26), extending Pilbara Hub life by 5+ years
Emerging Energy/gas business in the Perth and Carnarvon basins, monetized via the Hancock Prospecting transaction and continued exploration upside
Three-platform strategy (optimise existing operations, disciplined domestic growth, careful international expansion) leveraging the Mining Services capability into new commodities/jurisdictions
Capital Allocation Framework and organic deleveraging (net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.7x by end FY26, below the 2.0x target) creating headroom for growth investment and reinstated dividends

business.description: Iron ore and lithium prices directly drive ~two-thirds of segment earnings; lithium price collapse in FY24-FY25 (US$500-600/t spodumene) materially compressed earnings and management has admitted it 'got the lithium price wrong'
Nearly all operations are in Western Australia (Pilbara/Yilgarn), exposing the company to regional infrastructure, weather (cyclones) and labour market risk
Onslow Iron haul road damage during commissioning required remediation; future growth (Lamb Creek, international expansion) carries similar delivery risk
Iron ore and spodumene sales are heavily weighted to Chinese steel and battery supply chains

financial.description: Net debt was still ~$4.3-4.9bn through FY26 (materially down from FY25 peaks); leverage now 1.7x net debt/EBITDA, below the 2.0x target, but sensitive to a renewed commodity downturn

Debt structure predominantly US$3,050M+ senior unsecured bonds; AUD:USD moves create non-cash translation gains/losses (e.g., $101M FX gain on net debt in 1H26) and cash-flow currency mismatch against AUD-reporting entity
Active refinancing (US$700M notes refinanced Oct 2025; US$1.3bn new notes issued in 2H26 at 6.00%/6.25%) shows access to capital markets but at a meaningfully higher coupon than legacy debt

regulatory.description: Multiple historical related-party arrangements involving founder/MD Chris Ellison (personal use of company resources, offshore equipment supplier interest undisclosed for over a decade) triggered board investigations, an $8.8M personal penalty and forfeited remuneration for Ellison, and an ASIC formal investigation
A shareholder class action has been filed in the Victorian Supreme Court alleging misconduct that artificially inflated the share price

ASIC concluded its investigation into alleged tax evasion/non-disclosure in September 2026 without imposing penalties on MinRes or Ellison, removing a major regulatory overhang, though the class action remains live

macro.risk: China steel demand / iron ore price cycle
macro.description: Iron ore price (Platts 62% IODEX ~US$100-108/dmt through FY26) is sensitive to Chinese construction/steel demand and global supply additions from majors
Lithium demand and pricing are tied to the pace of global EV adoption and battery/ESS build-out; 2026 forecasts point to a market moving into deficit, but prior cycles show this can reverse quickly
High absolute debt load makes interest expense sensitive to global rate levels, though bonds are fixed-rate, long-tenor with no near-term maturities before late 2027

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Iron ore: mature, China-demand-driven market with ample seaborne supply from majors; MinRes' Onslow Iron differentiates on low cost and long life rather than market growth. Lithium: after a severe 2023-2025 price collapse, spodumene prices rose sharply through 2026 (roughly +57% YTD to around US$2,400/t by mid-2026) with forecasters projecting the market moving into deficit in late 2026, a favourable set-up for hard-rock producers like MinRes. Mining services/contract mining benefits from continued Pilbara and broader WA resources capital investment.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High for the Iron Ore and Lithium segments (direct commodity price exposure); Mining Services is structurally more resilient due to long-life, indexed contracts, acting as a stabiliser across the cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — large absolute debt balance but fixed-rate bonds with no maturities before late 2027 and no financial maintenance covenants limit near-term refinancing/rate risk
key_input_costs: Labour (FIFO workforce, competitive WA labour market)

recent_developments.event: FY26 full-year results: revenue $6,461M (+44% YoY), statutory NPAT $1,061M (+217% YoY, vs prior-year loss), NTA per share $24.02 (up from $18.67); Board declared a fully franked final dividend of $0.83/share — the first dividend since FY22

Net debt/EBITDA leverage fell to 1.7x, below the company's 2.0x target, driven by Onslow Iron and Mining Services cash flow plus improved H2 lithium prices; year-end liquidity of $2.4bn against a $1bn Board-set minimum

Formal execution of investment and shareholders' agreements with POSCO Holdings for a lithium JV: POSCO to pay ~US$765M upfront for a 30% interest (indirect 15% in each of Wodgina and Mt Marion), implying ~$3.9bn value for MinRes' existing 50% interests; completion expected in H1 FY27

ASIC concluded its formal investigation into Chris Ellison and MinRes over alleged undisclosed related-party dealings/tax matters, deciding not to pursue enforcement action, though the earlier internal board-imposed penalties on Ellison ($8.8M personal repayment, forfeited remuneration) and a shareholder class action remain

Chris Ellison's planned mid-2026 departure/transition was walked back; the Board scrapped the original succession timeline after concluding an internal candidate (via a newly created COO role held by 17-year MinRes veteran Darren Killeen) represents the lowest-risk succession path, with no fixed departure date for Ellison

Board substantially renewed with five new independent non-executive directors since May 2025 (including Chair Malcolm Bundey, Lawrie Tremaine, Ross Carroll), external governance review completed with King & Wood Mallesons, most legacy related-party transactions resolved or transitioning to competitive tender, and a new Capital Allocation Framework adopted

Bald Hill lithium mine restarted, making MinRes the world's only operator of three hard-rock lithium mines each with dedicated spodumene concentrate facilities; Onslow Iron reached 35Mtpa nameplate in August 2025 and is progressing toward ~40Mtpa
Sale of the legacy Yilgarn Hub iron ore assets after 14 years of operation, refocusing the iron ore portfolio on Onslow Iron and the Pilbara Hub

guidance.as_of: FY26 Annual Report / Q3-Q4 FY26 updates (August 2026)

items.notes: Driven by 6th and 7th transhippers arriving in 2026; FOB costs trending to the low end of the $54-59/wmt guidance range
Targeting close to $1bn in annualised EBITDA once Onslow Iron is at full run-rate; FY26 Mining Services Underlying EBITDA was $976M
Further deleveraging expected from POSCO transaction proceeds (~US$765M) on completion in H1 FY27

items.target: $0.83/share fully franked final dividend for FY26
items.notes: Signals Board confidence in balance sheet strength and earnings durability

items.target: Costs to decline as production shifts from Wonmunna to Lamb Creek
items.notes: Lamb Creek to extend Pilbara Hub mine life by 5+ years with less than two-year payback

items.target: Expected to rise modestly in 2H26 on lower-grade feed before improving as mining progresses to higher-grade zones
items.notes: 1H26 FOB costs were $726/dmt (Wodgina) and $805/dmt (Mt Marion), down sharply YoY on improved recoveries

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Malcolm Bundey: MinRes enters FY27 with 'a sound balance sheet, a resilient and growing Mining Services business, organic growth at Onslow Iron, Wodgina and Bald Hill, a renewed Board, embedded governance improvements and a clear leadership succession pathway.' MD Chris Ellison highlighted 'every division meeting or exceeding guidance' in FY26 and flagged Onslow Iron progressing beyond nameplate toward 40Mtpa in FY27, with the COO appointment (Darren Killeen) reflecting confidence in the internal leadership succession process. Management continues to describe Mining Services as the 'non-cyclical' earnings anchor and Onslow Iron as a 'generational asset' underpinning organic deleveraging.

bull_case: Record FY26 results (revenue +44%, NPAT +217%) with all three core segments — Mining Services, Iron Ore and Lithium — simultaneously performing well, and leverage already below the 2.0x target at 1.7x
Onslow Iron is a low-cost, long-life, high-margin asset still ramping toward ~40Mtpa, providing a multi-decade cash flow base that supports continued deleveraging and Mining Services growth

Lithium price recovery through 2026 (spodumene up sharply, market seen moving into deficit late 2026) directly re-rates the Wodgina/Mt Marion/Bald Hill portfolio just as the POSCO transaction (~US$765M) is set to complete and validate asset value (~$3.9bn implied for existing 50% stakes)

Governance overhang substantially reduced: Board fully renewed with five new independent directors, King & Wood Mallesons review completed and implemented, most related-party arrangements resolved, ASIC investigation concluded with no penalties, and a credible internal succession candidate (COO Darren Killeen) in place

Dividend reinstated ($0.83/share fully franked) after a three-year hiatus, signalling management/Board confidence and providing a fresh income data point for a stock previously seen as pure balance-sheet-risk
bear_case: Two of three core segments (iron ore, lithium) remain fully exposed to volatile commodity cycles; management has previously admitted misjudging the lithium price, and a renewed downturn would quickly pressure the balance sheet again

Chris Ellison remains Managing Director with no fixed departure date after the Board scrapped its original mid-2026 succession timeline — leadership uncertainty and founder key-person risk persist despite governance remediation

A shareholder class action alleging share-price-inflating misconduct remains outstanding even though ASIC closed its own investigation without penalties — legal/reputational tail risk is not fully resolved

Still-elevated absolute net debt (multiple billions of dollars, predominantly USD bonds) leaves the balance sheet more levered than diversified major peers (BHP, Rio Tinto, Fortescue), with refinancing at meaningfully higher coupons (6.00-6.25% on FY26 issuance) than legacy debt

Heavy concentration in Western Australia and predominantly Chinese offtake markets, plus execution risk on the next wave of growth (Lamb Creek, international expansion platforms), leaves limited diversification cushion if any single project underperforms
